evidence: The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks row 51 (sheet row 52) and its Internal Quality Checks annotation require well-formed TOML, LF bash scripts and reference entry syntax; the frozen skill quality-checks.md:204-206 additionally calls for seed parsing. Independent parser-results.json records 23 successful checks: seven TOML files (task, scoring and five judges), three JSON files, two Python ASTs, two bash -n checks (exit 0; zero CR bytes), and nine node --check invocations (exit 0). embedded-and-controls.json additionally parses the three test.sh Python heredocs, generated restart shell (test.sh:127-184), and solve.sh inline Node code. Entry server.js:2 resolves src/index.js; index.js:2-4 loads bootstrap; runtime dependencies and Node 22 are present in the declared Dockerfiles. Raw hash-verification.json confirms all six cited indexed artifacts and all 29 recorded source hashes equal the frozen bytes. Installed RewardKit discover/build_prompt/schema and OS argument-construction evidence in local/configured-inspection/results.json (SHA256 846bbc329dd21dae7950550587f858211460d50d6820ae5b459b52f38449b808) parses all five judges, resolves placeholders, and returns argument_launch_exit=0 (functional max argument 109199 bytes). Its driver explicitly launches /usr/bin/true with the constructed arguments, so this is not a provider grade. local/batch-ui/server.log records [hireops] listening on 3061; its source-bound driver launches the actual server.js and its results record successful browser operations and zero browser errors, supporting compatibility with the image Node v22.23.2 beyond local Node v24.19.0 syntax checks. All frozen source hashes were rechecked unchanged before writing this report. This Pass is limited to row 51; it does not establish private checker execution, full configured judge completion, reward behavior, Oracle/model score or task clearance.
counterexample: Assessed parser alternatives in embedded-and-controls.json: a broken entry require('./src/index.js'; is rejected with SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list (exit 1), while a conforming differently structured CommonJS bootstrap using const start = () => require('./src/index.js'); start(); parses (exit 0). A syntactically valid static/dead app could pass row 51, but that is the intended limit of a syntax row rather than evidence of reward acceptance; app behavior remains for other assigned checks. No syntax-based false failure of the conforming alternative was observed.
